title: Human causes of landform change

match.reason: The bank point only covers mining, quarrying and urban development, while the new point also needs dams, farming and land clearing as causes of landform change, so it is broader and would need new content rather than small edits.

draft.title: Human causes of landform change
card: People change landforms in two main ways. Some activities reshape the land directly. Others speed up erosion, which is the wearing away and moving of soil and rock by wind, water and gravity.
Mining and quarrying dig out rock and soil, leaving pits and cuts. Building levels ground and covers it with roads and concrete. Dams hold back a river and flood the land behind the wall.
Land clearing removes trees and plants whose roots hold soil together. Farming, such as ploughing or too many animals grazing, can leave soil bare. Wind and rain then carry it away faster.
These changes can happen in months or years. Natural processes usually take far longer to make the same change.
draft.remember: People change land directly by digging, building and damming, and can speed up erosion by removing plants that hold soil.

a.q: A farmer in north-west Victoria clears a hillside of trees to plant crops. How can this change the landform?
opts: Bare soil can be washed away faster by rain
The hill is dug out and leaves a large pit
A river is held back and floods the valley
The hill is levelled and covered with concrete
a.why: Tree roots hold soil in place, so clearing leaves bare soil that rain can wash away faster. Digging out a pit describes mining or quarrying, which is a direct change and not what clearing does.
a.clue: Think about what tree roots do to soil.

b.q: A company opens a quarry in the hills near Bendigo and removes rock for roads. Which describes how this changes the landform?
opts: It directly digs out rock and leaves a pit or cut
It speeds up erosion by taking plants off the soil
It holds back a river and floods land upstream
It levels ground and covers it with roads and houses
b.why: A quarry removes rock from the ground, so it changes the landform directly by leaving a pit or cut. Taking plants off soil is how clearing and some farming speed up erosion, which is not the main change a quarry makes.
b.clue: What is physically taken out of the hill?

a.best: Bare soil can be washed away faster by rain

b.best: It directly digs out rock and leaves a pit or cut
